name: Moped
description: A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with no external shifting device and a motor that can't propel it faster than 30 mph on a level surface; the statute lets the motor be electric. An electric two-wheeler past the electric assisted bicycle limits that tops out at 30 mph lands here, unless it has pedals and stops at 20 mph. Defined by N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(27)j.
restrictions: Two or three wheels, no external shifting device, and a motor that can't propel it faster than 30 mph on a level surface
The motor may be powered by electricity; the definition's 50 cc piston-displacement cap sets no wattage limit
Not an electric assisted bicycle or a motor-driven bicycle; one that can go faster than 30 mph is a motorcycle
Not a motor vehicle unless a statute says otherwise
Riders must be 16 or older to ride on a highway or public vehicular area
No driver's license or motorcycle endorsement needed
Riders and passengers must wear a safety helmet meeting FMVSS 218, with the retention strap secured
Carries no more people than it was designed for
Registered and plated with the DMV; no title or inspection
Must carry liability insurance of at least $30,000/$60,000/$25,000
